title: django-api
description: Request, latency and database behaviour of django-api, from django-prometheus's in-process instrumentation, with Traefik's edge view at the bottom for comparison. Provisioned by roles/argocd_django -- edits made in the UI are overwritten on the next Ansible run.

panels.title: Requests
panels.description: Requests per second Django itself handled, across every selected view. Static files are served by the nginx sidecar and never reach Django, so they are not counted here — see the Traefik row for the edge view.

panels.title: Server errors
panels.description: Share of responses with a 5xx status. These are Django's own failures — a request that never reached Django (upstream timeout, pod down) is a 5xx at Traefik but invisible here.

targets.expr: 100 * sum(rate(django_http_responses_total_by_status_view_method_total{job=~"$job", view=~"$view", view!="prometheus-django-metrics", method=~"$method", status=~"5.."}[$__rate_interval])) / sum(rate(django_http_responses_total_by_status_view_method_total{job=~"$job", view=~"$view", view!="prometheus-django-metrics", method=~"$method"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Client errors
panels.description: Share of responses with a 4xx status. A steady baseline of 401s is normal here — unauthenticated API probes — so watch for changes rather than the absolute number.

targets.expr: 100 * sum(rate(django_http_responses_total_by_status_view_method_total{job=~"$job", view=~"$view", view!="prometheus-django-metrics", method=~"$method", status=~"4.."}[$__rate_interval])) / sum(rate(django_http_responses_total_by_status_view_method_total{job=~"$job", view=~"$view", view!="prometheus-django-metrics", method=~"$method"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Latency p50
panels.description: p50 of Django request processing time over the selected views. Measured inside Django's middleware stack, so it excludes time spent queueing in gunicorn and time on the wire.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le) (rate(django_http_requests_latency_seconds_by_view_method_bucket{job=~"$job", view=~"$view", view!="prometheus-django-metrics", method=~"$method"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Latency p95
panels.description: p95 of Django request processing time over the selected views. Measured inside Django's middleware stack, so it excludes time spent queueing in gunicorn and time on the wire.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(django_http_requests_latency_seconds_by_view_method_bucket{job=~"$job", view=~"$view", view!="prometheus-django-metrics", method=~"$method"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Latency p99
panels.description: p99 of Django request processing time over the selected views. Measured inside Django's middleware stack, so it excludes time spent queueing in gunicorn and time on the wire.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(django_http_requests_latency_seconds_by_view_method_bucket{job=~"$job", view=~"$view", view!="prometheus-django-metrics", method=~"$method"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Response time percentiles
panels.description: Quantiles interpolated from django-prometheus's histogram buckets, which run 10ms → 75s. A percentile is only as precise as the bucket it lands in, so read the shape rather than the exact figure. The mean is drawn dashed: a mean that stays flat while p99 climbs means a small number of requests got much slower, which is the usual signature of one bad endpoint or a slow query.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le) (rate(django_http_requests_latency_seconds_by_view_method_bucket{job=~"$job", view=~"$view", view!="prometheus-django-metrics", method=~"$method"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.9, sum by (le) (rate(django_http_requests_latency_seconds_by_view_method_bucket{job=~"$job", view=~"$view", view!="prometheus-django-metrics", method=~"$method"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(django_http_requests_latency_seconds_by_view_method_bucket{job=~"$job", view=~"$view", view!="prometheus-django-metrics", method=~"$method"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(django_http_requests_latency_seconds_by_view_method_bucket{job=~"$job", view=~"$view", view!="prometheus-django-metrics", method=~"$method"}[$__rate_interval])))

sum(rate(django_http_requests_latency_seconds_by_view_method_sum{job=~"$job", view=~"$view", view!="prometheus-django-metrics", method=~"$method"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum(rate(django_http_requests_latency_seconds_by_view_method_count{job=~"$job", view=~"$view", view!="prometheus-django-metrics", method=~"$method"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Response time distribution
panels.description: Every request bucketed by how long it took, one column per time step. Latency spikes show up as colour moving up the y axis; a bimodal band (fast rows plus a second band higher up) usually means one endpoint or one code path is slow rather than the whole app.

panels.title: Requests slower than…
panels.description: Share of requests that crossed each threshold. This is read straight off the histogram buckets rather than interpolated, so unlike the percentile panel these numbers are exact. Useful as an SLO view: pick the line that matches what you promise and watch it, not p99.

targets.expr: 1 - (sum(rate(django_http_requests_latency_seconds_by_view_method_bucket{job=~"$job", view=~"$view", view!="prometheus-django-metrics", method=~"$method", le="0.25"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum(rate(django_http_requests_latency_seconds_by_view_method_bucket{job=~"$job", view=~"$view", view!="prometheus-django-metrics", method=~"$method", le="+Inf"}[$__rate_interval])))

1 - (sum(rate(django_http_requests_latency_seconds_by_view_method_bucket{job=~"$job", view=~"$view", view!="prometheus-django-metrics", method=~"$method", le="1.0"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum(rate(django_http_requests_latency_seconds_by_view_method_bucket{job=~"$job", view=~"$view", view!="prometheus-django-metrics", method=~"$method", le="+Inf"}[$__rate_interval])))

1 - (sum(rate(django_http_requests_latency_seconds_by_view_method_bucket{job=~"$job", view=~"$view", view!="prometheus-django-metrics", method=~"$method", le="2.5"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum(rate(django_http_requests_latency_seconds_by_view_method_bucket{job=~"$job", view=~"$view", view!="prometheus-django-metrics", method=~"$method", le="+Inf"}[$__rate_interval])))

1 - (sum(rate(django_http_requests_latency_seconds_by_view_method_bucket{job=~"$job", view=~"$view", view!="prometheus-django-metrics", method=~"$method", le="10.0"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum(rate(django_http_requests_latency_seconds_by_view_method_bucket{job=~"$job", view=~"$view", view!="prometheus-django-metrics", method=~"$method", le="+Inf"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: p95 by view
panels.description: The late-endpoint hunt. Each line is one Django view's own p95. A view that is slow but rarely called will show here and stay invisible in the overall percentiles above — cross-check it against "Time spent by view" below to decide whether it is worth fixing.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, view) (rate(django_http_requests_latency_seconds_by_view_method_bucket{job=~"$job", view=~"$view", view!="prometheus-django-metrics", method=~"$method"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Endpoint breakdown
panels.description: One row per view and method, averaged over the dashboard's whole time range (not the last sample), sorted slowest p95 first. "Time spent" is seconds of request processing per second of wall clock — rate × mean latency — which is the honest measure of which endpoint is actually costing the service: a 3s view called once an hour ranks below a 300ms view called ten times a second. Sort by it to find what to optimise; sort by p95 to find what feels slow.

targets.expr: sum by (view, method) (rate(django_http_requests_latency_seconds_by_view_method_count{job=~"$job", view=~"$view", view!="prometheus-django-metrics", method=~"$method"}[$__range]))

histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, view, method) (rate(django_http_requests_latency_seconds_by_view_method_bucket{job=~"$job", view=~"$view", view!="prometheus-django-metrics", method=~"$method"}[$__range])))

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, view, method) (rate(django_http_requests_latency_seconds_by_view_method_bucket{job=~"$job", view=~"$view", view!="prometheus-django-metrics", method=~"$method"}[$__range])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, view, method) (rate(django_http_requests_latency_seconds_by_view_method_bucket{job=~"$job", view=~"$view", view!="prometheus-django-metrics", method=~"$method"}[$__range])))
sum by (view, method) (rate(django_http_requests_latency_seconds_by_view_method_sum{job=~"$job", view=~"$view", view!="prometheus-django-metrics", method=~"$method"}[$__range]))

100 * sum by (view, method) (rate(django_http_responses_total_by_status_view_method_total{job=~"$job", view=~"$view", view!="prometheus-django-metrics", method=~"$method", status=~"5.."}[$__range])) / sum by (view, method) (rate(django_http_responses_total_by_status_view_method_total{job=~"$job", view=~"$view", view!="prometheus-django-metrics", method=~"$method"}[$__range]))

100 * sum by (view, method) (rate(django_http_responses_total_by_status_view_method_total{job=~"$job", view=~"$view", view!="prometheus-django-metrics", method=~"$method", status=~"4.."}[$__range])) / sum by (view, method) (rate(django_http_responses_total_by_status_view_method_total{job=~"$job", view=~"$view", view!="prometheus-django-metrics", method=~"$method"}[$__range]))

panels.title: Request rate by view
panels.description: Stacked, so the top of the stack is total throughput. A step change in one band with the total flat means traffic moved between endpoints; a step in the total means the callers changed.

panels.title: Server errors by view
panels.description: 5xx responses per second, by view. Anything appearing here is a Django exception or an explicit 5xx — pair it with the exception panels below to get the traceback type.

targets.expr: sum by (view) (rate(django_http_responses_total_by_status_view_method_total{job=~"$job", view=~"$view", view!="prometheus-django-metrics", method=~"$method", status=~"5.."}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Time spent by view
panels.description: Seconds of Django processing per second of wall clock, stacked. This is where the service's time actually goes. The total across all views approaches gunicorn's concurrency limit when the app is saturated — with a single sync worker, a sustained total near 1 means requests are queueing and every endpoint will look slow at the edge regardless of its own cost.

panels.title: Responses by class
panels.description: The four status classes. Read this first when something breaks: a 5xx band means Django failed, a 4xx band means the callers are being turned away, and a total that drops to nothing means traffic stopped reaching Django at all.

targets.expr: sum(rate(django_http_responses_total_by_status_view_method_total{job=~"$job", view=~"$view", view!="prometheus-django-metrics", method=~"$method", status=~"2.."}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)
sum(rate(django_http_responses_total_by_status_view_method_total{job=~"$job", view=~"$view", view!="prometheus-django-metrics", method=~"$method", status=~"3.."}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)
sum(rate(django_http_responses_total_by_status_view_method_total{job=~"$job", view=~"$view", view!="prometheus-django-metrics", method=~"$method", status=~"4.."}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)
sum(rate(django_http_responses_total_by_status_view_method_total{job=~"$job", view=~"$view", view!="prometheus-django-metrics", method=~"$method", status=~"5.."}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Responses by status code
panels.description: The same traffic split by exact code, which is what tells 401 from 403 and 502 from 504.

panels.title: Exceptions by view
panels.description: Unhandled exceptions django-prometheus counted as they propagated out of a view. These should be flat at zero; every step up is a traceback in the pod log worth reading.

panels.title: Exceptions by type
panels.description: The same exceptions grouped by Python exception class — usually enough to tell a database timeout from a bad request payload without opening the logs.

panels.title: Response body size percentiles
panels.description: How big the responses are. A latency spike that lines up with a size spike is a payload problem (an unpaginated list endpoint, a serializer pulling in too much) rather than a slow query.

panels.title: Requests by method
panels.description: Write traffic (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) against reads. Useful context for the database panels below.

panels.title: Query rate
panels.description: Statements executed per second, from django-prometheus's wrapped database backend. Divide by the request rate to get queries per request — a number that jumps after a deploy is the classic N+1 regression.

panels.title: Query duration percentiles
panels.description: Time per statement. When request p95 climbs and this climbs with it, the problem is in Postgres or the network to it; when this stays flat, the time is being spent in Python.

panels.title: Connections and errors
panels.description: New database connections per second, plus failures. Django opens a connection per request unless CONN_MAX_AGE is set, so a connection rate tracking the request rate is expected here — what matters is the error lines staying at zero.

panels.title: Time spent in the database
panels.description: Seconds of query time per second of wall clock, and how many statements the average request runs. Compare the first against "Time spent by view": when they move together the app is waiting on Postgres, and when queries-per-request jumps after a deploy without the traffic changing, something lost its select_related and is issuing a query per row.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: Share of cache reads that found something. A page cache that is working should sit high and steady; a ratio that collapses after a deploy usually means the cache key changed rather than that the cache broke. Needs two things the app is not doing yet: CACHE_URL is unset, so Django falls back to a per-process LocMemCache and the memcached Deployment beside it goes unused; and django-prometheus only counts cache operations when CACHES uses its wrapper backend (django_prometheus.cache.backends.*), the way DATABASES already uses django_prometheus.db.backends in fkweb/settings/base.py. Until both land this row stays empty.

panels.title: Cache operations
panels.description: Reads, hits, misses and failures per second by cache backend. The gap between gets and hits is what the cache is costing rather than saving; failures are the backend being unreachable, which Django swallows and turns into a miss. Needs two things the app is not doing yet: CACHE_URL is unset, so Django falls back to a per-process LocMemCache and the memcached Deployment beside it goes unused; and django-prometheus only counts cache operations when CACHES uses its wrapper backend (django_prometheus.cache.backends.*), the way DATABASES already uses django_prometheus.db.backends in fkweb/settings/base.py. Until both land this row stays empty.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio by backend
panels.description: The same ratio as the stat, split per backend and over time. Read it next to "Time spent by view": a view that got slower at the same moment this dipped is being served from the database instead of the cache. Needs two things the app is not doing yet: CACHE_URL is unset, so Django falls back to a per-process LocMemCache and the memcached Deployment beside it goes unused; and django-prometheus only counts cache operations when CACHES uses its wrapper backend (django_prometheus.cache.backends.*), the way DATABASES already uses django_prometheus.db.backends in fkweb/settings/base.py. Until both land this row stays empty.

panels.title: Unapplied migrations
panels.description: From django_migrations_unapplied_total. Non-zero means the running code expects a schema the database does not have — a failed or half-finished deploy. start.sh runs migrate on boot, so this should only ever be zero.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Time since the gunicorn worker started. A reset here explains a discontinuity in every counter on this dashboard, and an uptime that keeps resetting is a crash loop.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: CPU seconds burned per second by the Django process. With a single sync gunicorn worker this saturates at 1 core — at that point latency is queueing, not slow code, and the fix is more workers rather than a faster endpoint.

panels.title: Memory and file descriptors
panels.description: Resident memory and open file descriptors. Memory that only ever climbs between restarts is a leak; file descriptors climbing usually means connections are not being closed.

panels.title: Edge requests by status
panels.description: The same traffic as seen by Traefik, before it reaches Django. Two differences matter: /static is answered by the nginx sidecar and never appears in the Django panels above, and a 502/504 here with no matching 5xx above means Django never answered at all — the pod was down, restarting, or the request timed out in the queue.

panels.title: Edge requests slower than…
panels.description: Traefik measures the whole request including queueing and the response body transfer, so this is what a client actually experiences. Traefik's default histogram is only four buckets wide (0.1, 0.3, 1.2, 5s), which is why this shows bucket shares rather than percentiles — an interpolated p95 off four buckets would be fiction. A gap between these lines and the Django-side thresholds is time spent queueing rather than working.
